I'll use serum/plasma ALT concepts (the common clinical ones: 3006923, 3005755, 3027388) plus blood variants. The key challenge is the ULN — OMOP stores it in `range_high` on the measurement row. I'll flag ALT > 2× `range_high`. Let me run the full analysis.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH iso_desc AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS drug_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 984232
),
alt_concepts AS (
  SELECT concept_id FROM (VALUES (3006923),(3005755),(3027388),(46235106),(46236949),(36032251),(3000784)) v(concept_id)
),
-- first isotretinoin start per person
iso_start AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS start_date
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN iso_desc d ON d.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
-- adolescents: age 10-19 at isotretinoin start
adol AS (
  SELECT s.person_id, s.start_date,
         DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,1), ISNULL(p.day_of_birth,1)), s.start_date) AS age_at_start
  FROM iso_start s
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = s.person_id
),
cohort AS (
  SELECT * FROM adol WHERE age_at_start BETWEEN 10 AND 19
),
-- ALT measurements within 90 days after start, with a valid numeric value and a positive ULN (range_high)
alt_m AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, m.value_as_number, m.range_high,
         CASE WHEN m.range_high IS NOT NULL AND m.range_high > 0
                   AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
                   AND m.value_as_number > 2.0 * m.range_high
              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS alt_gt2uln
  FROM cohort c
  JOIN omop.measurement m ON m.person_id = c.person_id
  JOIN alt_concepts a ON a.concept_id = m.measurement_concept_id
  WHERE m.measurement_date >= c.start_date
    AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day, 90, c.start_date)
    AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
    AND m.range_high IS NOT NULL AND m.range_high > 0
),
per_person AS (
  SELECT person_id, MAX(alt_gt2uln) AS ever_gt2uln
  FROM alt_m
  GROUP BY person_id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cohort) AS adolescents_started_isotretinoin,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) FROM alt_m) AS with_alt_measured_90d,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM per_person WHERE ever_gt2uln = 1) AS with_alt_gt2uln_90d

content.text: 1,818 adolescents were started on isotretinoin, but **zero** had an ALT measurement with a populated reference range (`range_high`) in the 90 days after start. That means the `> 2× ULN` calc using per-row ULN yields 0 — the ULN field isn't populated in this dataset. Let me verify whether ALT is measured at all and check how the range is stored.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH iso_desc AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS drug_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 984232
),
alt_concepts AS (
  SELECT concept_id FROM (VALUES (3006923),(3005755),(3027388),(46235106),(46236949),(36032251),(3000784)) v(concept_id)
),
iso_start AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS start_date
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de JOIN iso_desc d ON d.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
cohort AS (
  SELECT s.person_id, s.start_date
  FROM iso_start s JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = s.person_id
  WHERE DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,1), ISNULL(p.day_of_birth,1)), s.start_date) BETWEEN 10 AND 19
),
alt_m AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, m.value_as_number, m.range_high, m.unit_concept_id
  FROM cohort c
  JOIN omop.measurement m ON m.person_id = c.person_id
  JOIN alt_concepts a ON a.concept_id = m.measurement_concept_id
  WHERE m.measurement_date >= c.start_date AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day, 90, c.start_date)
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS alt_rows_90d,
  COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS persons_with_alt_90d,
  SUM(CASE WHEN value_as_number IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_with_value,
  SUM(CASE WHEN range_high IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_with_range_high,
  SUM(CASE WHEN range_high IS NOT NULL AND range_high > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_range_high_pos
FROM alt_m

The reference range (`range_high`/ULN) is essentially unpopulated: of 1,302 ALT rows across 856 adolescents in the 90-day window, only **1** row has any `range_high` and **none** has a positive value. So a strict per-row `> 2× ULN` rule is unanswerable from stored data.

The clinically standard fallback is a fixed ULN. ALT ULN for adolescents is ~40 U/L, so 2× ULN = **80 U/L** (units are essentially all U/L here). Let me confirm units and compute against the 80 U/L threshold.

WITH iso_desc AS (

  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 984232

  SELECT concept_id FROM (VALUES (3006923),(3005755),(3027388),(46235106),(46236949),(36032251),(3000784)) v(concept_id)
),

  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS start_date
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de JOIN iso_desc d ON d.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
cohort AS (
  SELECT s.person_id, s.start_date
  FROM iso_start s JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = s.person_id
  WHERE DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,1), ISNULL(p.day_of_birth,1)), s.start_date) BETWEEN 10 AND 19
),
alt_m AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, m.value_as_number, m.unit_concept_id,
         CASE WHEN m.value_as_number > 80.0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS gt80
  FROM cohort c
  JOIN omop.measurement m ON m.person_id = c.person_id
  JOIN alt_concepts a ON a.concept_id = m.measurement_concept_id
  WHERE m.measurement_date >= c.start_date AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day, 90, c.start_date)
    AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
),

  SELECT person_id, MAX(gt80) AS ever_gt80 FROM alt_m GROUP BY person_id

  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cohort) AS cohort_n,

  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM per_person WHERE ever_gt80=1) AS persons_gt80,

## Answer

Among adolescents (age 10–19 at their first isotretinoin exposure), ALT elevation > 2× ULN within 90 days is recorded in **11 of 1,818** patients — about **0.6%** overall, or **1.3%** (11/856) of those who actually had ALT checked in that window.

### Important caveat on the ULN
A literal "> 2× the recorded ULN" is **not answerable** from this database: of the 1,302 ALT results in the 90-day window, only 1 row had any `range_high` populated and none had a positive value. I therefore used a **fixed pediatric threshold of 2× ULN ≈ 80 U/L** (ULN ~40 U/L, values are in U/L). If your ULN convention differs, the count will shift.

### Cohort definition used
- **Drug**: first `drug_exposure` for any descendant of isotretinoin ingredient (`concept_id 984232`).
- **Adolescent**: age 10–19 at that first exposure.
- **Lab**: serum/plasma/blood ALT LOINC concepts, `value_as_number` between index date and +90 days.
- **Denominators**: 1,818 started isotretinoin; **856 (47%) had any ALT drawn** in 90 days — so monitoring itself is incomplete.

| Metric | n | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Adolescents started on isotretinoin | 1,818 | — |
| …with any ALT in 90 days | 856 | 47.1% |
| …with ALT > 2× ULN (≈80 U/L) in 90 days | 11 | 0.6% of all / 1.3% of tested |

Two honest limitations: the recorded reference range is essentially empty (fixed 80 U/L used as a surrogate), and fewer than half of these adolescents had ALT monitored at all within 90 days.
